documents.title: Palladium-catalyzed directing group assisted and regioselectivity reversed cyclocarbonylation of arylallenes with 2-iodoanilines

Palladium-catalyzed directing group assisted and
regioselectivity reversed cyclocarbonylation of
arylallenes with 2-iodoanilines †
Jian-Shu Wang,‡a Lingyun Yao,‡a Jun Ying,
 *a Xiaoling Luo*b and
Xiao-Feng Wu
 *a,c
A palladium-catalyzed regioselective cyclocarbonylation of N-(2-pyridyl)sulfonyl ( N-SO2Py)-2-iodoani-
lines with allenes has been developed. With the assistance of the directing group N-SO2Py, the regio-
selectivity of arylallenes was reversed and the reaction proceeded well to give various 3-methylene-2,3-
dihydroquinolin-4(1H)-ones with up to 95% yield by using benzene-1,3,5-triyl triformate (TFBen) as the
CO source. Control experiments and DFT calculations were performed to understand the reaction details
and a possible reaction mechanism is proposed accordingly.
Introduction
2,3-Dihydroquinolin-4(1H)-ones are considered as a type of
crucial structural motif existing in many molecules with
diverse biological activities such as analgesic, 1 anti-tumor,2,3
and immunosuppressive properties. 4 In addition, they are
important building blocks for the construction of valuable
heterocyclic compounds. 5,6 Owing to their useful skeletons, a
variety of synthetic methods to access 2,3-dihydroquinolin-4
(1H)-ones have been realized. 7,8 Among all the 2,3-dihydroqui-
nolin-4(1H)-ones, 3-methylene-2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1 H)-ones
are a special class and usually have been prepared by the con-
densation of 2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1 H)-ones with aldehydes.
Hence, new alternative methodologies for their preparation are
always in demand.
Transition-metal-catalyzed carbonylative reactions have
been recognized as one of the most straightforward and
eﬃcient methods to synthesize carbonyl-containing com-
pounds.
9 Additionally, the chemistry of allenes in synthetic
preparations is quite versatile.10 Numerous novel synthetic pro-
cedures have been established. However, the reports on the
carbonylative transformation with allenes are still limited com-
pared with the reports on that with alkenes or alkynes. 11,12 The
possible reasons are due to the high reactivity of allenes and
the related regioselectivity issues.
Among the achievements, in 2007, Alper and Ye reported an
attractive palladium-catalyzed ionic-liquid-promoted carbony-
lative cyclization of 2-iodoanilines with allenes. 12 Various
3-methylene-2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1H)-ones were produced in
moderate to good yields under 5 bar of CO (Scheme 1a). 12 This
reaction occurred selectively at the 1,2-position of the alkyl
substituted allenes applied. Under their conditions, buta-2,3-

Herein, we report a new palladium-catalyzed cyclocarbonyla-
tion of ( N-SO
2Py)-2-iodoanilines with allenes. With the assist-
ance of the directing group, the regioselectivity was reversed
and the reaction occurred only at the 2,3-position of the arylal-
lenes applied. Various 3-methylene-2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1 H)-
ones were produced in good yields with excellent regio-
selectivities by using TFBen
13 as the CO source (Scheme 1b).
Results and discussion
Initially, ( N-SO2Py)-2-iodoaniline 1a and allene 2k were
selected as the model substrates with TFBen (4.0 equiv.) as the
CO source in the presence of Pd(OAc) 2 (10 mol%), and various
phosphine ligands were tested in dioxane at 90 °C for 24 h
(Table 1, entries 1 –5). Gratifyingly, using DPPP as the ligand
with an appropriate bite angle, the reaction gave the cyclocar-
bonylated regiomers 3ak and 3ak′ in 35% isolated yield with a
ratio of 1 : 1 (Table 1, entry 4). Next, a series of solvents were
investigated (Table 1, entries 6 –9). It was found that employing
MeCN as the solvent could enhance the yield (41%) and regio-
selectivity (5 : 1) (Table 1, entry 6). Notably, with the use of
toluene, the target product 3ak as a single regiomer was
obtained in 53% yield (Table 1, entry 7). Subsequently, several
palladium catalyst precursors were tested in this reaction
(Table 1, entries 10 –13). The reaction with Pd(acac)
2 improved
the yield of 3ak to 61% (Table 1, entry 12). Remarkably, the
yield was increased to 87% when the reaction system was
diluted (Table 1, entry 14). Additionally, 70% yield of the
product 3ak could be achieved even when using only 1 mol%
of Pd(acac)
2 (Table 1, entry 15). It was noteworthy that the reac-
tion yield was maintained (85%) when the amount of TFBen
was reduced to 1.0 equivalent (Table 1, entry 16).
With the optimal reaction conditions (Table 1, entry 16) in
hand, we turned to investigate the scope of allenes 2 in the
reaction with ( N-SO2Py)-2-iodoaniline 1a (Scheme 2). The reac-
tion with phenylallene 2a gave the expected product 3aa in
87% yield, whose structure was unambiguously confirmed by
X-ray crystallography (CCDC 2023302, see the ESI †).14
Phenylallenes bearing either para-electron-donating or
para-electron-withdrawing substituents could undergo the
reaction smoothly to give the corresponding products 3ab–ai
in high yields (69 –95%). It was shown that the reaction with
meta-substituted phenylallenes proceeded well to a ﬀord the
desired products 3aj–an in excellent yields (85 –91%).
Furthermore, good yields of the products 3ao–aq were
obtained when phenylallenes with ortho-substituents such as
Me, Cl, and Br were tested. For 2,5-dimethyl phenylallene 2r,
the reaction led to the product 3ar in 88% yield. Additionally,
naphthylallene 2s could be converted into the desired product
3as in an excellent yield (93%). Notably, when 1,1- or 1,3-di-
substituted allenes were subjected to the reaction system, a
series of the target products 3at–aw were achieved in good
yields (73 –93%). Aliphatic allene was tested as well, and 74%
yield of the corresponding product 3ax was obtained. However,
the reaction occurred at the 1,2-position in this case.
Subsequently, a variety of ( N-SO
2Py)-2-iodoanilines 1 were
prepared and tested in the reaction with phenylallene 2a
(Scheme 3). For the substrates bearing functional groups such
as Me, MeO, F, CF 3, COMe, COOMe, and Ph at the C4 position,
the reaction a ﬀorded the corresponding products 3ba–ha in
high to excellent yields (80 –93%). Moreover, the compounds
having substituents such as Cl and Br at the C5 position were
successfully converted into the desired products 3ia and 3ja in
88% and 93% yields, respectively. It was also found that the
reaction with di-substituted compounds could lead to the pro-
ducts 3ka and 3la in high yields as well.
In order to show the utility of this protocol, a series of trans-
formations of the product 3aa were accomplished to furnish
diverse 2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1 H)-ones with important func-
tional moieties (Scheme 4). 15 The dibromination of 3aa in the
presence of N-bromosuccinimide and benzoic acid as the cata-
lyst at 50 °C for 24 h a ﬀorded dibromo compound 4 in 90%
yield (Scheme 4, eqn (1)). When 3aa was treated with benzyl
amine mediated by I 2/TBHP at room temperature, 75% yield of
aziridine 5 was obtained (Scheme 4, eqn (2)). Additionally, 3aa
was transformed into dicarbonyl compound 6 in 87% yield via
the thiazolium-catalyzed Stetter reaction (Scheme 4, eqn (3)).
To our delight, when compound 6 was treated with excess
zinc powder in a mixed solvent (THF/NH 4Cl(aq) = 1 : 1), the
removal of the N-SO2Py directing group was realized in a facile

Next, we studied the e ﬀect of directing groups on 2-iodoani-
lines in the carbonylation with phenylallene 2a, and the
results are shown in Scheme 6. Initially, it was found that the
reactions with unprotected 2-iodoaniline 8, Me-2-iodoaniline
9, and Boc-2-iodoaniline 10 gave complicated mixtures without

the expected cyclocarbonylated products (Scheme 6, eqn (1)–(3)).
When Ac-2-iodoaniline 11 was subjected to the standard con-
ditions, 80% of aldehyde 12 was obtained and the target product
13 was not observed (Scheme 6, eqn (4)). Interestingly,
N-benzenesulfonyl-2-iodoaniline14 could undergo the reaction
to give the cyclocarbonylated regiomers15 and 15′ with a signifi-
cantly reduced yield (31%) and regioselectivity (6 : 1), which
suggested that the coordination of the palladium catalyst with
the N atom on N-SO2Py of 2-iodoanilines was crucial in this reac-
tion (Scheme 6, eqn (5)). Finally, the reaction did not occur
when N-picolinyl-2-iodoaniline16 was tested, indicating that the
sulfuryl unit on the directing group also played an important
role in promoting the cyclocarbonylation (Scheme 6, eqn (6)).
In order to have a better understanding of the reaction
pathway, a possible reaction intermediate 17 was prepared and
tested under our standard conditions (Scheme 7). The reaction
of compound 17 with or without phenylallene 2a under the
standard reaction conditions produced intramolecular Heck
cyclization product 18 in 80% or 30% yield, respectively. In both
cases, the cyclocarbonylated product 3aa was not observed.
These findings showed that the carbonylation step was probably
prior to the reaction of the NH group with allenes.
According to the experimental observation and previous
theoretical studies
16 on the mechanism, two possible pathways
for this palladium-catalyzed cyclocarbonylation of 2-iodoani-
lines with allenes are proposed (Scheme 8). The reaction starts
from DPPP-coordinated Pd(0) species A, which is produced
from Pd(acac) 2 with phosphine or CO as the reductant and
then reacts with 2-iodoanilines by oxidative addition to a ﬀord
aryl Pd( II) intermediate B. Next, CO insertion into the Pd –C
(aryl) bond gives rise to acylpalladium intermediate C as the
common initiation of the two pathways. In path I, allene
migratory insertion occurs into the Pd –C(carbonyl) bond fol-
lowed by intramolecular transformation to generate allylpalla-
dium complex D, which can undergo deprotonation by the
extra base NEt 3 to a ﬀord allylpalladium species E. Subsequent
nucleophilic addition gives cyclocarbonylation product 3.
Alternatively, for path II, acylpalladium intermediate C can
undergo deprotonation first to a ﬀord five-membered pallada-
cycle F, followed by allene migratory insertion into the Pd –C
(carbonyl) bond forming seven-membered palladacycle G.
Reductive elimination provides the same product 3 finally.
To understand the mechanism and the regioselectivity of
the palladium-catalyzed cyclocarbonylation of 2-iodoanilines
with allenes, we performed a detailed DFT investigation. The
calculated results of the favored path are shown in Fig. 1.
The catalytic cycle begins with the oxidative addition of the
aryl iodide moiety of 1 to active Pd(0) catalyst 19 and generates
coordinative intermediate 20, which is exergonic by 8.6 kcal
mol
−1. The energy of intermediate 20 is set as the zero point
for the whole catalytic cycle. Oxidative addition of the aryl
iodamide moiety occurs via three-membered-ring transition
state 21-ts to form aryl Pd(
II) intermediate 22, which is strongly
exergonic by 29.0 kcal mol −1. The activation free energy for
this step is 10.4 kcal mol −1. Then, CO replaces the iodide and
coordinates with the central palladium atom to give species
23, followed by CO insertion into the Pd –C(aryl) bond via
three-membered-ring transition state 24-ts to form carbonyl-
palladium compound 25. This process is exergonic by
15.5 kcal mol −1 and the barrier is 13.5 kcal mol −1.
Subsequently, allene 2 replaces the iodide and coordinates
with the central palladium atom to form π-coordinative inter-

the Pd –C(carbonyl) bond then occurs via transition state 27-ts
with an activation free energy of 29.3 kcal mol −1 to form alkyl-

3, proton transfer

regeneration of active species 20 to accomplish the full cata-

insertion step with an activation free energy of 29.3 kcal
mol−1. Path II was calculated to be unfavored and the details
are shown in Fig. S1. †
The regioselectivity was also considered for this reaction. As
shown in Fig. 2, in the allene insertion process, allene 1,2-
insertion into the Pd –C(carbonyl) bond can proceed via tran-
sition state 33-ts to a ﬀord the corresponding byproduct 35.
The relative free energy of 33-ts is 2.5 kcal mol
−1 higher than
that of 27-ts relative to allene 2,3-insertion, which indicates
that the 2,3-insertion product 3 is the main product thermo-

dynamically and kinetically. In order to illustrate the origin of
regioselectivity, distortion –interaction energy analysis of the
transition states 27-ts and 33-ts was performed and the calcu-
lated results are presented in Table 2. The distortion energy of
the allene moiety is 19.0 kcal mol −1 in 27-ts and 24.5 kcal
mol−1 in 33-ts, whereas the distortion energies of the carbonyl-
palladium part and the interaction energies are similar.
Correspondingly, the ∠CvCvC of the allene moiety in 27-ts
and 33-ts is 143.1° and 136.5°, respectively. It confirms that
more distortion of the allene moiety in 33-ts results in a
higher activation energy in the migratory insertion process.
Conclusions
In conclusion, we have developed a facile and e ﬃcient
approach to access various 2,3-dihydroquinolin-4(1 H)-ones in
good yields and with excellent regioselectivities via a palla-
dium-catalyzed cyclocarbonylation of ( N-SO2Py)-2-iodoanilines
with allenes using TFBen as the CO source. This transform-
ation can be realized successfully owing to the e ﬀect of the
N-SO
2Py directing group. Control experiments and DFT calcu-
lations were performed to understand the reaction pathway.
Experimental
General procedure
(N-SO2Py)-2-iodoaniline 1 (0.5 mmol, 1.0 equiv.), Pd(acac) 2
(0.05 mmol, 10 mol%), DPPP (0.05 mmol, 10 mol%), and a
2.5 mL vial containing TFBen (0.5 mmol, 1.0 equiv.) were
added to an oven-dried tube (15 mL) which was then placed
under vacuum and refilled with nitrogen three times. Allene 2
(1.25 mmol, 2.5 equiv.), Et 3N (1.0 mmol, 2.0 equiv.) and
toluene (2.5 mL) were added into the tube via a syringe. The
tube was sealed and stirred at 90 °C for 24 h. After the reaction
was completed, the resulting mixture was concentrated under
vacuum and purified by silica gel column chromatography
( petroleum ether/ethyl acetate = 5 : 1) to obtain the product 3.
